summary: Salmon National Forest lookout in Lemhi County; a 1935 newspaper item names Lynn Thomas in charge. No later record found.

events.note: Recorder Herald item dated August 7, 1935 reports a new lookout established at Poison Peak. It gives no design or build details.
Same item: the paper understood Lynn Thomas to be in charge. This is the only staffing name found.

evidence.supports: 1935 item: new lookout established at Poison Peak, Lynn Thomas in charge
evidence.quote: A new lookout has been established at Poison peak back of the Edson ranch, we understand with Lynn Thomas in charge.

evidence.supports: 1935 marked the peak of lookouts in the forest, with 34 standing
evidence.quote: 1935 appears to have marked the time when lookouts reached their peak. Thirty-four lookouts then stood as sentinels over the forest.

evidence.supports: 1929 was one of the worst fire years, particularly with the Wilson Creek Fire
evidence.quote: The year 1929 was one of the worst fire years in the recorded history of the Salmon National Forest, particularly with the Wilson Creek Fire.

evidence.supports: The forest began a large lookout construction program
evidence.quote: enabled the Forest to initiate a massive lookout construction program

evidence.supports: The 1929 fires, including Wilson Creek, pushed the forest to improve detection
evidence.quote: In order to avoid large conflagrations of the size of the Wilson Creek Fire, the early detection system needed additional improvement.

evidence.supports: Depression-era workers made the lookout program possible
evidence.quote: coupled with the surfeit of workers made available by the Great Depression

sources.title: An Overview of the Lookouts in the Salmon National Forest, Bing Young (1982)

notes_for_editor: Only one source names the lookout: a 1935 newspaper item quoted on Kemnow's page. The text of the 1982 Bing Young overview does not name Poison Peak. The county and coordinates come from the existing record; a map-site search snippet (not fetched) places Poison Peak near Elk Bend in Lemhi County. The forest may now be called Salmon-Challis; the Forest Service history page I fetched does not confirm a rename, so it is not used. No design, construction date, fate or current status was found.
